slot.subtopic: Tense consistency (simple past vs present perfect)
slot.brief: Give a sentence where present perfect is misused with a finished-time marker ('yesterday'); ask for the corrected version among four rewrites.

stem: Choose the best improvement for the underlined part of the sentence: The committee <u>has announced its decision yesterday</u>.
options: The committee has announced its decision yesterday.
The committee announced its decision yesterday.
The committee had announced its decision yesterday.
The committee announces its decision yesterday.

verdicts.working: “Yesterday” specifies a completed past time, so use the simple past: “announced.”

working:
“Yesterday” marks a finished time, so use the simple past: “announced.” Present perfect does not pair with this marker; past perfect needs another past reference point; simple present is inconsistent with “yesterday.”

solution: “Yesterday” indicates a completed past time, so the simple past tense is required: “announced.”
